items.title: A flat injective epimorphism out of a ring of weak dimension at most one lands in an integral extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring A of weak dimension at most one and a flat, injective epimorphism of rings A -> B, and asserts that A is integrally closed in B (source lines 30705-30710). The proof is a cancellation argument. Let x in B be integral over A and set A' = A[x], a subring of B; then A' is a finite ring extension of A by the Algebra characterization of finiteness in terms of integrality (proof lines 30713-30715). To show A = A' it suffices to show that A -> A' is an epimorphism, by the Algebra statement that a finite epimorphism is surjective (proof lines 30716-30717). The key input is that A' is flat over A, which follows from the hypothesis on A together with the flatness of B over A (proof lines 30718-30719). The proof then exhibits the composition A' tensor_A A' -> B tensor_A A' -> B tensor_A B -> B and concludes it is injective (proof lines 30720-30724), which says A' tensor_A A' is isomorphic to A' and hence A -> A' is an epimorphism, completing the proof (proof line 30724). The non-routine content is the flatness of the intermediate ring A' over A, which is what supplies the injectivity of the tensor product map, and the reduction of the integrality claim to the surjectivity of a finite epimorphism.
